title: Move grounding-freshness verification from tag-push gate to ordinary CI
context: Stale grounding docs (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, etc.) went undetected in ordinary CI because the only check ran exclusively on TAG PUSH in the release gate. Commits from other machines, CI with --no-verify, or clones without hooks installed carried stale docs all the way to the irreversible tag step. This cost two red cycles on 2026-08-09 (fnd_6391b4242f).
decision: Add a deterministic test that runs on every commit, regenerates the hunch grounding section (PUBLIC-ONLY, no overlay), compares against committed CLAUDE.md, and fails with an actionable fix command. Deliberately excludes symbol/edge counts (platform-dependent) and includes only RECORD counts from .hunch/*.json (platform-invariant).
consequences: Grounding staleness caught in ordinary CI with exact reproduction steps, not at the irreversible tag step
Developers learn the precise regeneration command without decoding release-gate error messages
HUNCH_PRIVATE_DIR precedence enforced in test, preventing private overlays from polluting committed public docs
Determinism across Windows/Linux by excluding symbol/edge counts while verifying RECORD counts
Release gate no longer fails on stale-grounding issues
alternatives_rejected: Keep verification only at tag-time gate (original design) — expensive, detected after commit is irreversible, failure message unclear
Include symbol/edge count checks — would flap due to legitimate platform differences (2793 vs 2792)
Broaden hook coverage to catch all commit paths — doesn't help --no-verify, other machines, or clones without hooks installed
Static/AST verification of grounding — overengineered when .hunch/*.json is the authoritative source
